q-22237.name: Question 1
q-22237.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $b.$ To do this, we treat $c$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $4b$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}b-5c & =c-4b \\ b-5c+4b & =c-4b+4b \\ b+4b-5c & =c-4b+4b \\ 5b-5c & =c\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we add $5c$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5b-5c & =c \\ 5b-5c+5c & =c+5c \\ 5b & =6c\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5b & =6c \\ \frac{5b}{5} & =\frac{6c}{5} \\ \frac{\cancel{5}b}{\cancel{5}} & =\frac{6c}{5} \\ b & =\frac{6c}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we add 4b to both sides of the equation:

b−5c=c−4bb−5c+4b=c−4b+4bb+4b−5c=c−4b+4b5b−5c=c

q-135011.name: Question 2
q-135011.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $z.$ To do this, we treat $y$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $2y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z}{3}-2y & =1 \\ \frac{z}{3}-2y+2y & =1+2y \\ \frac{z}{3} & =1+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply both sides of the equation by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z}{3} & =1+2y \\ 3\cdot \frac{z}{3} & =3\cdot (1+2y) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot \frac{z}{\cancel{3}} & =3\cdot (1+2y) \\ z & =3\cdot (1+2y) \\ z & =3\cdot 1+3\cdot 2y \\ z & =3+6y\end{aligned}
$$

q-176587.name: Question 3
q-176587.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ To do this, we treat $y$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y & =y-x \\ 2x-y+y & =y-x+y \\ 2x & =-x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we add $x$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-x+2y \\ 2x+x & =-x+2y+x \\ 3x & =2y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =2y \\ \frac{3x}{3} & =\frac{2y}{3} \\ \frac{\cancel{3}x}{\cancel{3}} & =\frac{2y}{3} \\ x & =\frac{2y}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
